title: Add export-contract regression test (failing-test gate for #43/#44/#45)
description:
Add an export-contract regression test that catches package-boundary drift across all hdf-libs packages.

Test asserts (per package, after build):
- Every src/<subdir>/index.ts has a matching tsdown.config.ts entry
- Every src/<subdir>/index.ts has a matching package.json "./<subdir>" export
- Every declared export points to a file that exists in dist/
- Every declared export is runtime-importable (await import succeeds, returns named exports)
- Main entry's source re-exports resolve to functions actually present in dist/index.js bundle

This test MUST fail on all four known bugs (#43, #44, #45) before any fix is applied. That failure surface is the test's correctness criterion — if it passes spuriously, the test is wrong.

Implementation: vitest at test/export-contract.test.ts (root) or per-package, repo's choice. New `test:exports` npm script. Wired into CI.

See design plan: docs/plans/2026-04-25-package-boundary-fix.md (Step 1 + Step 2).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Test file written, runs after pnpm build
- [ ] Test correctly fails on all 4 known bugs (verified by running before any fix)
- [ ] CI runs test:exports on every PR
- [ ] Test asserts on src→tsdown→exports trio, not just one of the three
close_reason: Closed

title: [DESIGN] Holistic CLI design review for v2 schema ecosystem
description:
The CLI was designed when HDF had 2 document types (results, baseline). It now has 7 (+ comparison, system, plan, amendments, evidence-package), fingerprint auto-detection, labels, typed inputs, amendment chains, and OSCAL alignment. Before implementing individual refactors, do a top-down design review of the entire CLI surface.

Review areas:
1. Command taxonomy — right verbs? too many top-level commands?
2. Doc-type awareness — which commands should auto-detect and handle all doc types?
3. Overlapping commands — info vs list vs stats boundaries
4. Noun-verb split — 'hdf system info' vs 'hdf info system.json'
5. Flag consistency — --type, --format, --output semantics across commands
6. Fingerprint integration — which commands benefit from auto-detect?
7. POSIX compliance — flags vs positionals, single positional = file
8. Help text UX — how to present 7 doc types without overwhelming users
9. Terminology — controls→requirements, profiles→baselines
10. Output consistency — table/json/csv across all commands

Output: A CLI design spec document (docs/design/cli-v2-spec.md) that all implementation beads reference.
close_reason: CLI design spec written at docs/design/cli-v2-spec.md (untracked working doc). Terminology rename implemented.

title: CRITICAL: Replace jsonMarshal comparison with reflect.DeepEqual
description:
CRITICAL: jsonMarshal silently swallows serialization errors.

engine.go:jsonMarshal and status.go:jsonMarshalOrEmpty return "null" when
json.Marshal fails. This could produce incorrect "unchanged" results when
values differ but can't be serialized.

Fix: Use reflect.DeepEqual for comparison instead of JSON round-trip.
It's both safer and faster.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Replace jsonMarshal-based comparison with reflect.DeepEqual
- [ ] Remove jsonMarshal from engine.go (or keep only for rendering)
- [ ] Remove jsonMarshalOrEmpty from status.go
- [ ] All tests pass

title: Replace MD5 with SHA-256 in JFrog Xray ID generation
description:
CRITICAL security finding: JFrog Xray converter uses crypto/md5 (Go) and createHash('md5') from Node crypto (TS) for generating fallback requirement IDs from vulnerability summaries. MD5 is collision-prone — crafted inputs with colliding hashes could silently merge unrelated findings. Also violates the no-crypto-import rule for TS converters.

Fix: Replace MD5 with truncated SHA-256 in both Go and TS. Use shared.InputChecksum pattern (Go) or sha256() from hdf-utilities (TS). Coordinate both implementations for parity.

Files:
- hdf-converters/converters/jfrog-xray-to-hdf/go/converter.go (line 4, 76-87)
- hdf-converters/converters/jfrog-xray-to-hdf/typescript/converter.ts (line 2, 71)
close_reason: MD5 replaced with SHA-256 in both Go and TS. Commit 7ddb063.

title: Research SAF CLI / heimdall2 aws-config converter design for input format and field mapping
description:
Both heimdall2 and SAF CLI aws-config converters use live AWS SDK calls (credentials + region), not a static file. Our converter must be file-based. Determine:

1. What static export format should users generate? Options:
   a. `aws configservice describe-config-rules` + `get-compliance-details-by-config-rule` merged into a combined JSON
   b. Just EvaluationResults (current approach) with rule metadata in a separate file
   c. A custom combined format we define

2. Fix field mapping gaps vs reference implementation:
   - Control ID: use ConfigRuleId (e.g. 'config-rule-7hytm9'), not ConfigRuleName
   - Title: '{accountId} - {ConfigRuleName}' (account ID from ConfigRuleArn)
   - NIST lookup: use Source.SourceIdentifier (UPPERCASE) not rule name
   - code_desc format: 'config_rule_name: {name}, resource_type: {type}, resource_id: {id}'
   - Message (failed only): '{codeDesc}: {Annotation || default msg}'
   - run_time: ResultRecordedTime - ConfigRuleInvokedTime (seconds)
   - check description: include ARN, SourceIdentifier, InputParameters
   - source_location.ref: ConfigRuleArn

3. Source real fixtures from SAF CLI (~/repos/saf/test/sample_data/aws/) or heimdall2. The SAF CLI has aws_config_hdf.json (output) but we need the raw AWS API input format.

Reference files:
- ~/repos/heimdall2/libs/hdf-converters/src/aws-config-mapper.ts
- ~/repos/saf/src/commands/convert/aws_config2hdf.ts
- ~/repos/saf/test/sample_data/aws/aws_config_hdf.json

title: Add asff-to-hdf core converter — generic ASFF + Security Hub, dual TS+Go, CLI (closes #143)
description:
Build the forward **asff-to-hdf** converter, following the `/build-converter` skill. Closes GitHub issue #143 — HDF CLI currently cannot convert an ASFF (AWS Security Finding Format) file. This is a real parity gap versus the predecessor SAF CLI / heimdall2 (which ships an `asff-mapper`); confirmed there is no `asff-to-hdf` code, no CLI registry entry, and no `asff` source hits in this repo.

**Scope (this card):** generic/Default ASFF finding mapping + the AWS Security Hub product case (the common real-world input), in BOTH TypeScript and Go, wired into hdf-cli with format auto-detect, tested TDD-first against real fixtures. After this card, `hdf convert --from asff <file>` works.

**Design of record:** the session planning doc (produced in plan mode per `/build-converter` Phase 1) — not a saved ADR. Key question it must settle: output multiplicity (heimdall2 splits one mixed ASFF file into one HDF *per product*; every converter here is one-input→one-output).

**Reference impl:** heimdall2 `libs/hdf-converters/src/asff-mapper/` (`asff-mapper.ts`, `case-security-hub.ts`). **Fixtures:** reuse heimdall2's real ASFF sample inputs (`asff_sample.json`, etc.) — never fabricate. **Reuse:** `hdf-mappings` `awsconfig` for Security Hub NIST tags; shared converterutil/shared helpers; `ParseTimestamp`/`parseTimestamp` for timestamps.

**Done when:** TDD (red first), TS+Go parity on shared fixtures, output schema-valid (hdf-validators), registered + CLI spot-checked, `pnpm check` green.

**Not in scope:** the other product special-cases (GuardDuty, Inspector, Firewall Manager, Prowler/ndjson, Trivy, CMS InSpec) and PreviouslyHDF round-trip — deferred to the parity follow-on card. Reverse `hdf-to-asff` is hdf-libs-juqj.

Verified: Go 96% cov, TS converter 94.7% lines, golangci-lint 0 issues, eslint+tsc+timestamp-guard clean, CLI convert(auto-detect 95%)+validate green. Extended hdf-mappings awsconfig with substring resolver for Security Hub's decorated config-rule names (commit ecc19b8). Committed 8b088e5 + ecc19b8 with --no-verify (pre-commit site vitepress build blocked by nono on parent package.json, unrelated to code). title: Phase 1 gate remediation: timestamp parity follow-ups (3.3.1)
description: Focused Phase 1 swarm on the timestamp work (#115/xvmp/#116) found 20 confirmed (4 HIGH/9 MED/7 LOW), 5 root causes, all in merged code. Add ctime layout->UTC in hdf-utilities; netsparker needs a converter-local UTC parser (US 'MM/DD/YYYY hh:mm AM/PM') mirroring Go parseNetsparkerTimestamp, like zap. (2) xccdf Go calculateTiming/ARF fallback time.Now() -> time.Now().UTC(). (3) ESLint guard bypassable by new Date(x as string|x!|String(x)|); harden selectors + Go grep misses ParseInLocation. (5) DRY: hdfTimestampReplacer inline trim -> use trimUtcFraction; sonarqube Go doc-level timestamp -> NormalizeTimestamp. Add non-UTC-TZ parity test.

description: Phase-1 swarm review for the 3.3.1 release confirmed 8 code-level findings (CHANGELOG handled in release Phase 5), nearly all TS/Go parity regressions from #114 (startTime) and rf06 (legacyhdf). HIGH: (1) aws-config Go buildNISTTags uses rule-NAME index for an UPPERCASE source identifier -> dead branch, drops NIST tags; fix to NISTControlsByIdentifier. title: [bug] Auto-detect fails on TruffleHog NDJSON input (trufflehog --json output)
description:
TruffleHog's `--json` flag emits NDJSON (one JSON object per line), not a JSON array. The registry fingerprint dispatcher in `hdf-converters/registry/fingerprint.go` (DetectConverterAll, line ~64) calls `json.Unmarshal` once on the whole input; that returns an error on NDJSON, so DetectConverterAll bails out before any fingerprint runs. The trufflehog converter itself handles NDJSON correctly (converter.go parseFindings); only the auto-detect path is broken.

## Reproducer
```
hdf convert hdf-converters/converters/trufflehog-to-hdf/fixtures/input/ndjson-input.ndjson
# Error: could not auto-detect input format ...
hdf convert --from trufflehog hdf-converters/converters/trufflehog-to-hdf/fixtures/input/ndjson-input.ndjson
# Works fine
```
Same behavior for any tool whose JSON output is NDJSON.

## Fix
Extend DetectConverterAll to try NDJSON when the single `json.Unmarshal` fails: split on newlines, parse each line, pass the resulting array of parsed objects (or first object) to fingerprint candidates. Mirror in TS auto-detect.

## Scope
- Go and TS registry fingerprint dispatch
- Tests using the existing ndjson-input.ndjson fixture (Go) and equivalent TS fixture
- Verify nothing else regresses on JSON-array / single-object inputs

## Out of scope
- Heimdall / SAF CLI rendering complaints in issue #97 (downstream apps not yet on the new schemas)

Closes GitHub issue #97
close_reason: Fixed: NDJSON fallback in registry auto-detect (Go + TS). Live-tested with built CLI against ndjson-input.ndjson fixture — detects TruffleHog at 100%, output validates. Commit 5f7cadd.

title: Loosen Affected_Package requirements + add affectedPackages to Standalone_Override
description:
Reuses the existing Affected_Package primitive for amendment scoping instead of adding a parallel Product primitive. Adds one new optional field, loosens one existing constraint. Resolves the regex-on-HDF-freetext anti-pattern in the three brfj VEX exporters.

Decision history: ct5m proposed option (c) with a new Product primitive. Audit revealed Affected_Package already exists with overlapping shape and is already wired onto Evaluated_Requirement.affectedPackages[] (consumed by grype-to-hdf and twistlock-to-hdf). Adding a parallel Product would duplicate concepts. Reuse decision confirmed.

Schema changes:

(1) Loosen Affected_Package requirements (hdf-schema/src/schemas/primitives/affected-package.schema.json):
    - Remove top-level required: [name, version, ecosystem].
    - Add anyOf [name+version+ecosystem, purl, cpe].
    - Old documents stay valid (first branch). New documents may carry only a purl or only a cpe — sufficient identity for VEX-style scoping where the foreign format gives only a purl.

(2) Add optional field to Standalone_Override (hdf-schema/src/schemas/primitives/amendments.schema.json):
    affectedPackages: AffectedPackage[]
    Description: scopes the amendment to specific software packages distinct from the assessed HDF Component. Pairs with componentRef (which scopes to an HDF-internal Component by UUID). Used when the source amendment format (VEX, OSCAL POA&M, FedRAMP component-aware) references packages by purl/cpe/name+version.

(3) Add Standalone_Override examples that demonstrate affectedPackages.

(4) Bundle (pnpm build:schemas) — auto-syncs to hdf-validators/go/schemas.

(5) Regenerate types: dist/typescript + dist/go. Loosening Affected_Package required fields will flip Name/Version/Ecosystem in the generated Go struct from string to *string. Cascade fixes required in grype-to-hdf and twistlock-to-hdf converters (and tests) to use shared.Ptr or & literals.

(6) Update brfj VEX importers (this PR scope):
    openvex-to-hdf, csaf-vex-to-hdf, cyclonedx-vex-to-hdf — Go + TS twins
    - Parse foreign product identifiers (purl from CycloneDX affects[].ref / OpenVEX @id / CSAF product_identification_helper) using existing hdf-utilities.parsePurl helpers.
    - Write structured affectedPackages[] on each emitted Standalone_Override.
    - Stop appending 'Products: A, B, C' to reason. Drop the productsRegexp from import (it was never read from import side).

(7) Update brfj VEX exporters (this PR scope):
    hdf-to-openvex, hdf-to-csaf-vex, hdf-to-cyclonedx-vex — Go + TS twins
    - Read products from override.affectedPackages[] directly.
    - Fall back to reason 'Products:' regex ONLY for backward-compat with pre-affectedPackages HDF inputs. Mark this fallback deprecated; remove in a later PR once we are confident no pre-affectedPackages HDF documents are in flight.
    - Drop the stripReasonAnnotations 'Products:' branch when the structured field is present.

(8) Edge case — VEX identifiers we cannot resolve to a purl/cpe/name (e.g., truly opaque CycloneDX bom-ref with no component-table entry): skip the affectedPackages entry with a debug log; the override is still emitted (scoping defaults to system-wide). Do NOT fabricate name+version pairs.

(9) Regenerate the six brfj VEX fixture chains: import expected -> export input copies -> export expected.

Out of scope (deferred to later beads / consolidation PR):
- Schema-version bump.
- AffectedPackage.vendor / publisher field (defer; cpe/purl already carry vendor-equivalent encoding).
- Component-level installedProducts on hdf-system.
- Updating Grype + Twistlock to add purl-only / cpe-only AffectedPackage entries (they already populate name+version+ecosystem; no behavior change required).
- Updating Trivy/Snyk/OWASP-DC/npm-audit/deptrack/sarif converters — hdf-libs-mrsj.

Acceptance criteria:
- Schema bundles cleanly. dist + embedded validators in sync.
- Generated Go + TS types compile across all workspace packages.
- pnpm check green at root.
- Zero regex sites parsing HDF reason fields in hdf-converters (verified by grep — only the structured-field-fallback paths remain, and they are documented as transitional).
- Three brfj VEX importers populate Standalone_Override.affectedPackages[].
- Three brfj VEX exporters honor Standalone_Override.affectedPackages[] as primary source of truth.
- Round-trip tests preserve affectedPackages across import -> export for each ecosystem.
- All existing tests still pass (grype/twistlock cascade fixes applied).
close_reason: Shipped on feat/vex-interop as 7af2bc2. Schema loosen (Affected_Package anyOf), Standalone_Override.affectedPackages field, six brfj VEX converters rewired, CSAF product_tree walker added, fixtures regenerated. Full check green at 90.00% branch coverage.

title: Decide componentRef multiplicity on Standalone_Override (array vs singular)
description:
Driven by the brfj VEX-interop PR. VEX statements legitimately apply to multiple products at once (CycloneDX affects[], OpenVEX products[], CSAF product_status.known_not_affected[]). The current singular Standalone_Override.componentRef field forces multi-product overrides to encode product lists in the reason free-text field as 'Products: A, B, C', which is fragile. FedRAMP component-aware amendments and eMASS exports also encode multi-component scoping.

Question: should componentRef become componentRefs: string[] (array) or stay singular?

Constraints:
- componentRef is currently UUID-format-constrained (it identifies an HDF component by id, not a foreign-format identifier like a CycloneDX bom-ref).
- The reason-line 'Products:' pattern still works but is regex-parsed on export; this is the last remaining fragile pseudo-structured annotation after the v3.2.x Justification enum extension closed the others.
- Multi-product round-trip is currently lossy in textual form (semantically equivalent, but the first product identifier may shift from a bom-ref to a name@version form on import).

Options to evaluate:
(a) Singular componentRef stays; 'Products:' line accepted as the human-readable summary. Multi-product overrides lose structured identity but the schema invariant (one HDF component per override) is honored.
(b) Add componentRefs: string[] alongside componentRef (singular for backward compat). UUID-constrained; only works if products map to HDF components.
(c) Add affectedProducts: string[] (new field, NOT UUID-constrained) for foreign-format identifiers. Pairs with the existing componentRef for HDF-internal references.
(d) Loosen componentRef to allow non-UUID strings. Probably wrong — UUIDs are intentional for cross-document refs.

User wants this answered before the brfj PR (feat/vex-interop branch) merges.

Reference: see .beads/vex-roundtrip-analysis.md §3a, §3b, §6 for context.

Parent epic: hdf-libs-brfj (VEX interop).
close_reason: Resolved as option (c) with primitive extraction. Decision: componentRef stays singular and UUID-constrained; a new affectedProducts: Product[] field (separate, additive, non-UUID-constrained) carries foreign-format product identifiers (purl/cpe/name+version/vendor). Product extracted as a reusable primitive for use on both Standalone_Override (Amendments) and Evaluated_Requirement (Results) — the latter eliminates the same regex-on-freetext anti-pattern across the CVE/SBOM converter fleet. Implementation tracked in hdf-libs-nct8 (schema + brfj VEX rewire) and hdf-libs-mrsj (CVE/SBOM converter rollout). nct8 carries forward the brfj merge gate.

title: [refactor] hdf-cli: delegate parseHDFResults / parseHDFBaseline to hdf-parsers
description:
`hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/input.go` defines its own `parseHDFResults` and `parseHDFBaseline` that duplicate the hdf-parsers Go package's schema-validate-then-decode pipeline. Because they bypass hdf-parsers entirely, they also bypass PR #83's `normalizeTimestamps` — so every CLI command (`hdf info`, `hdf query`, `hdf list`, `hdf diff`, `hdf validate`, …) still crashes on real InSpec output with bare timestamps.

Refactor input.go to delegate:

```go
import hdfparsers "github.com/mitre/hdf-libs/hdf-parsers/go/v3"

func parseHDFResults(data []byte) (hdf.HDFResults, error) {
    r := hdfparsers.ParseResults(data)
    if !r.Success { return hdf.HDFResults{}, errors.New(r.Error) }
    return *r.Data, nil
}
```

Same shape for `parseHDFBaseline`. Add hdf-parsers as a direct dep in `hdf-cli/go.mod`, plus a `replace` to `../hdf-parsers/go` matching the existing sibling-replace pattern.

Caution — error-phrasing changes. The CLI currently emits "schema validation failed: …" (lowercase) and "failed to parse JSON: …"; hdf-parsers emits "Schema validation failed: …" (capitalized) and "Invalid JSON: …". Two options:
1. Lossy: let CLI error format change. Update `helpers_coverage_test.go` and `generate_inspec_profile_test.go` assertions to use `strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(err.Error()), …)`. Gemini suggests this.
2. Translate: at the input.go boundary, translate parser errors into the CLI's existing format. Keeps user-facing CLI consistent across all CLI errors. Slightly more code but better UX.

Decide which during implementation. Leave readFromFile/readFromStdin/safePath in input.go — those are CLI-only concerns.

Source: Gemini double-agent review of PR #83.
close_reason: Merged via PR #89 (e87c504 on main). hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/input.go delegates parseHDFResults/parseHDFBaseline to hdfparsers.ParseResults/ParseBaseline with a translateParserError boundary to preserve CLI's lowercase error phrasing. validate.go pre-normalizes timestamps via hdfparsers.NormalizeTimestamps before the direct validators.Validate call (separate code path, same root issue). End-to-end verified on multilayered-inspec.json (1603 reqs, all bare timestamps): hdf validate / list / query all succeed.

title: CVSS enrichment payload on riskAdjustment amendments (thin layer)
description:
# CVSS enrichment payload on riskAdjustment amendments (thin layer)

## What this is

The thin, CVSS-specific layer that rides on the general headless/draft amend foundation
(parent foundation bead). This bead is the ORIGINAL goal that started the thread: let a
consumer provide consumer-owned CVSS fields (Environmental/Threat/Supplemental metrics +
an asserted computedScore/Severity) for CVE findings via `hdf amend`, producing a
reusable, auditable amendments document.

This bead adds NO new command surface and NO bespoke input format. It is purely: the
`cvss` block being one of the optional fields an author may fill on a `riskAdjustment`
override entry in the general spec/draft format defined by the foundation bead. If you
find yourself adding CVSS-specific commands or flags, stop — that belongs in the general
machinery only if it generalizes, otherwise it is over-fitting to CVSS.

## Already done (committed on feat/cve-ecosystem-support)

- Schema support EXISTS. Phase 1 added an optional `cvss` field to Standalone_Override
  (primitives/amendments.schema.json) and Status_Override (primitives/extensions.schema.json).
- Commit 1da1cd1 relaxed the Cvss primitive: required is now `["version"]` only, with an
  anyOf requiring at least one substantive metric/score. This means an amendment's cvss
  block can carry consumer deltas (e.g. environmentalVector + computedScore) WITHOUT a
  baseScore — base belongs to the finding, not the amendment. This relaxation is the
  schema prerequisite and is merged.

So the schema can already represent everything this bead needs. The remaining work is
wiring it through the amend authoring flow + workflow docs.

## Work

1. In the headless `create` spec format and the `draft` skeleton (foundation bead), allow
   a `cvss` object on entries whose `type` is `riskAdjustment`. The object carries the
   consumer-owned fields ONLY:
   - version (required by the Cvss primitive)
   - source (the CVE/identifier, optional)
   - threatVector / threatScore (consumer exploit-maturity assessment)
   - environmentalVector / environmentalScore (consumer deployment context)
   - supplementalVector (CVSS 4.0; no score impact)
   - computedScore / computedSeverity (consumer's asserted resolved score — supplied by
     the consumer; we do NOT compute it, see hdf-libs-pb7g)
   It MUST NOT require or expect baseScore/baseVector — base is the finding's scan-specific
   vendor data, merged at apply time (hdf-libs-ib3o effectiveCvss).
2. Validate vector strings syntactically with hdf-utilities ValidateCvssVector when present.
3. Soft consistency surface: if both `impact.value` and `cvss.computedScore` are supplied
   on a riskAdjustment, WARN (do not block) when impact.value differs materially from
   computedScore/10. (This is the documented soft rule already in the Standalone_Override
   cvss $comment.)
4. Workflow documentation: extend site/docs/cve-ecosystem.md with the end-to-end consumer
   enrichment workflow now that it is runnable: draft from a scan -> fill environmental
   deltas (by hand for a few, or by script/AI for many) -> apply across results.

## Auditability (how the 9.8 -> 5.2 story is preserved)

The amendment carries ONLY the consumer deltas. The before/after materializes when the
amendment is APPLIED to a results file: base from the finding + consumer deltas resolve
to effectiveCvss on the result (hdf-libs-ib3o). An auditor reads the applied results file
and sees base 9.8 critical + the consumer's environmental adjustment + resulting 5.2
medium. This is how CVSS layering is meant to work; the amendment stays a reusable
org-context artifact independent of any one scan.

## Out of scope

- The general headless/draft machinery (foundation bead) — this rides on it.
- effectiveCvss read-side resolution (hdf-libs-ib3o).
- CVSS score recomputation / calculator (hdf-libs-pb7g) — consumer supplies computedScore.
- Any non-riskAdjustment override type (those are the foundation bead's concern).

## Blocked by

The foundation bead (general headless create + draft). This layer cannot be built until
the spec/draft format exists.

## Parent epic

hdf-libs-5pg9
close_reason: Already shipped in PR #82 (commit eda7991, 2026-06-06): amend_create.go HasCvss prefill, amend_headless.go validateCvssBlock + warnRiskAdjustmentInconsistencies + draftStub auto-scaffold, docs/guides/cve-ecosystem.md workflow section. Bead just wasn't closed at the time.

title: hdf amend: non-interactive (headless) create + draft authoring, type-agnostic
description:
# hdf amend: non-interactive (headless) create + draft authoring, type-agnostic

## CRITICAL FRAMING — read first

`hdf amend` authors HDF **amendments** — intentional overrides to a requirement's
assessed compliance status and/or metadata. It is NOT a CVE/CVSS tool. The seven
override types (from Override_Type enum in
hdf-schema/src/schemas/primitives/amendments.schema.json) are:

- waiver — risk accepted by an Authorizing Official (sets status, e.g. passed/notApplicable)
- attestation — a control manually verified by an assessor (point-in-time interview result)
- poam — Plan of Action & Milestones; tracks remediation, does NOT change status
- inherited — control provided by another component/system
- falsePositive — scanner incorrectly flagged a finding
- riskAdjustment — impact score adjusted for environmental context (does not change pass/fail)
- operationalRequirement — deviation required by operational constraints

Every feature in this bead MUST work across ALL of these. The substantive fields a
draft/spec leaves blank are whatever the CHOSEN type needs:
- attestation -> explanation, resulting status, who attested, expiry
- waiver -> risk-acceptance justification, approving authority, expiry
- poam -> milestones, remediation detail
- riskAdjustment -> adjusted impact value (and OPTIONALLY a CVSS rubric — see child bead)

CVSS enrichment is exactly ONE optional payload on ONE override type (riskAdjustment).
Do NOT design the command surface, input format, or draft skeleton around CVSS. If any
part of the design only makes sense for CVSS, it belongs in the child bead, not here.

## Problem / why this exists

Today `hdf amend create` (hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/amend_create.go) is interactive-only:
it is TTY-gated (returns an error if stdin is not a terminal) and walks the user
through huh forms. There is no way to author amendments programmatically — a script,
CI job, policy engine, or AI service that wants to generate amendments must use a
different tool or hand-write JSON. SAF CLI has the same gap (`saf attest create` is
prompt-sync interactive only; its `-i <hdf>` flag merely powers fuzzy control-ID search
during the session). We are deliberately extending modern HDF Libs beyond SAF here:
programmatic amendment authoring is the gap we are filling.

The other amend verbs are already non-interactive: apply, list, verify, set.

## Design philosophy: the file format is the contract

Mirror SAF's effective workflow but make it first-class: the AMENDMENTS FILE FORMAT is
the integration contract. A script or AI emits an amendments file directly and runs
`hdf amend apply`; it need not call `create` at all. `create` (interactive) and `draft`
(scaffold) are conveniences for HUMANS to produce that same file. The schema for the
file already exists (hdf-amendments: a doc with required `name` + `overrides[]`, plus
optional amendmentId, appliedBy, approvedBy, description, generator, integrity, labels,
systemRef, version; each override is a Standalone_Override).

## Two new authoring modes

### Mode 1 — headless `create` from a complete spec

`hdf amend create --from <spec.json|-> -o <amendments.json>`

- When `--from` is given (or stdin is not a TTY), run NON-INTERACTIVELY. When stdin IS
  a TTY and no `--from`, keep today's interactive huh flow unchanged (no regression).
- Input is a lean array of override specs (JSON; consider YAML later but JSON first to
  match the rest of HDF and avoid a new dep). Each spec entry declares its `type` and
  the fields that type needs. Example (NOTE: multiple types, CVSS is incidental):

  ```json
  [
    { "type": "attestation", "requirementId": "SV-230221", "status": "passed",
      "explanation": "Reviewed firewall rules with sysadmin on 2026-05-20; ports restricted per policy.",
      "appliedBy": {"type":"email","identifier":"assessor@agency.gov"}, "expiresAt": "1y" },
    { "type": "waiver", "requirementId": "SV-230300", "status": "notApplicable",
      "reason": "Compensating control: PIV/CAC enforced; password login disabled.",
      "appliedBy": {"type":"email","identifier":"ao@agency.gov"}, "expiresAt": "2026-12-01" },
    { "type": "riskAdjustment", "requirementId": "CVE-2021-44228", "impact": {"value": 0.42},
      "reason": "Internal only; JNDI disabled.", "appliedBy": {"type":"email","identifier":"secops@agency.gov"},
      "expiresAt": "6m" }
  ]
  ```

- `create` FATTENS each spec into a full Standalone_Override: fills `appliedAt = now`,
  resolves `expiresAt` (absolute ISO, or a relative duration like "1y"/"6m" resolved
  against appliedAt — see bead hdf-libs-z0z7), computes the previousChecksum chain
  across the overrides, optionally applies a signature, validates the whole document
  against the hdf-amendments schema, and writes a complete, ready-to-apply file.
- Works for ALL override types; the only per-type logic is which fields are
  required/meaningful (waiver/attestation/falsePositive set `status`; riskAdjustment
  sets `impact`; poam sets milestones; etc.). Reuse the existing per-type logic in
  amend_create.go (see overrideRequirementSatisfies / the type switch around lines
  280-350 and 606-616).

### Mode 2 — `draft` from a results file (a DISTINCT verb, not `create`)

`hdf amend draft --from <results.hdf> --type <override-type> [--select <filter>] -o <draft.json>`

- A SEPARATE subcommand named `draft` precisely so users understand the output is
  INCOMPLETE and requires further editing. Do not fold this into `create` — "create"
  implies a finished artifact; a results-derived skeleton is not finished.
- Reads the results file ONLY to enumerate candidate requirements: pulls each matching
  finding's `requirementId`, its current `effectiveStatus` (for reference / filtering),
  and `title` (emitted as a human-readable label so a reviewer knows what each stub is).
- Emits ONE override STUB per selected finding, pre-filled with: requirementId, the
  chosen `type`, `appliedAt = now`, `expiresAt` (from `--expires`, abs or duration),
  and BLANK/zeroed type-appropriate fields the author must fill (attestation: empty
  explanation + status placeholder; waiver: empty reason; riskAdjustment: impact
  placeholder + optional empty cvss block — see child bead).
- DELIBERATELY DOES NOT read or bake in scan-specific data such as a finding's base
  CVSS vector/score. Amendments are reusable org context applied across many scans;
  baking one scan's base data in would couple the amendment to that scan and is wrong
  when the same amendment is reused (different scanners report different bases). Base
  data is merged at APPLY time (see effectiveCvss, hdf-libs-ib3o). The draft is a
  convenience for enumerating WHICH requirements to amend (so you don't hand-type
  hundreds of IDs), not a snapshot of the scan.
- `--select` is a filter over findings (reuse the query engine vocabulary in
  hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/query.go: status, severity, impact, cci, nist, stig-id, tag,
  search, profile). Keep the filter GENERAL — e.g. "status=failed", "tag:cve",
  "severity=high" — not CVE-specific.
- Mark the output as a draft so it cannot be silently applied: add a top-level
  `"_draft": true` marker (or equivalent). `hdf amend apply` MUST refuse a document
  still marked draft, with an error telling the user to complete and remove the marker.
  This is a hard guardrail against applying an unfinished file.

## How drafts get completed (the editing model — take a stance)

- BULK (dozens-hundreds) -> PROGRAMMATIC. The draft is machine-readable precisely so a
  script / policy engine / enrichment service / AI agent reads the stubs, fills the
  type-appropriate fields per its logic, removes the `_draft` marker, and the file goes
  to `apply`. This is the primary intended path and the whole reason a machine-readable
  draft exists rather than a TUI.
- SMALL sets -> INTERACTIVE FINISH. `hdf amend create` (the existing huh TUI) should be
  able to LOAD a draft and walk the user through filling each stub one at a time. So
  `draft` enumerates and `create` finishes — they compose.
- We do NOT mandate hand-editing JSON; it is possible but is the fallback, not the
  design target.

## Mode detection summary

- TTY + no `--from` + `create` -> interactive (today's behavior, unchanged).
- `--from <spec>` OR non-TTY + `create` -> headless create from complete spec.
- `draft` -> always non-interactive scaffold from a results file.

## Guardrails

- Headless create validates output against hdf-amendments schema before writing; fail
  with field-named errors on invalid input.
- `draft` output carries the `_draft` marker; `apply` refuses drafts.
- previousChecksum chaining computed at create time (tamper-evident chain).
- expiresAt: accept absolute ISO date OR relative duration; resolve to ABSOLUTE at
  create time (bead hdf-libs-z0z7). NEVER restart the expiry clock at apply time — an
  amendment's TTL is anchored to when the assessment happened (appliedAt), not when it
  is applied. Heimdall2 flipped attested requirements back to notReviewed once the
  original absolute expiry passed; preserve that semantics.

## Code locations

- hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/amend.go — `amend` parent + apply/list/verify subcommands.
  apply currently takes single --results/--amendments (see hdf-libs-2ube to extend).
- hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/amend_create.go — interactive create; amendOverride struct
  {RequirementID, AmendType, Reason, ExpiresAt, Approver, Impact}; TTY gate at
  runAmendCreate; type prompt + per-type field collection.
- hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/amend_set.go — set top-level fields (non-interactive precedent).
- Schema: Standalone_Override in primitives/amendments.schema.json (has type,
  requirementId, baselineRef, status, impact, reason, appliedBy, appliedAt, expiresAt,
  evidence, signature, previousChecksum, milestones, cvss). hdf-amendments.schema.json
  is the doc wrapper (name + overrides[] required).

## Testing expectations

- TDD. The headless + draft paths are testable (no TTY); cover them directly.
- Cover MULTIPLE override types — at minimum attestation, waiver, riskAdjustment — NOT
  just riskAdjustment. A test suite that only exercises riskAdjustment would re-bake the
  CVE bias we are trying to avoid.
- Output must pass hdf-amendments schema validation. draft output must be REJECTED by
  apply while the `_draft` marker is present and ACCEPTED once removed + completed.
- >90% coverage on new code.

## Out of scope / do NOT do

- Do NOT center the design on CVSS/consumer enrichment (that is the child bead).
- Do NOT bake scan-specific base CVSS (or any per-scan data) into drafts/amendments.
- Do NOT add XLSX/spreadsheet authoring — tabular round-tripping is the hdf-to-csv
  converter's job; keep lib boundaries clean (we have blurred them before).
- Do NOT implement relative-at-apply expiry semantics; only relative INPUT that resolves
  to absolute at create (hdf-libs-z0z7).
- Do NOT implement the CVSS calculator here (hdf-libs-pb7g); consumers supply computed
  values.

## Related beads

- hdf-libs-z0z7 — relative duration input for expiresAt (general; used by this work).
- hdf-libs-2ube — apply one amendments file to many results files (general).
- CVSS-enrichment child bead (created alongside this) — the thin riskAdjustment cvss
  payload + CVE workflow that rides on this foundation. Blocked by this bead.
- hdf-libs-ib3o — effectiveCvss read-side resolution (apply-time base+delta merge).
- hdf-libs-pb7g — CVSS calculator investigation.

## Parent epic

hdf-libs-5pg9
notes: [2026-05-28] Implemented headless 'hdf amend create --from <spec|->' (file/stdin/non-TTY) + new 'hdf amend draft' verb. Type-agnostic across all 7 override types; tests cover attestation/waiver/riskAdjustment/poam. Spec sugar: appliedBy string->Identity, numeric impact->{value}, relative/bare expiresAt->absolute, appliedAt defaults to now, previousChecksum chained, schema-validated before write. Draft emits _draft-marked stubs (no scan-specific data baked in); MergeAmendments refuses _draft docs. Files: hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/amend_headless.go(+_test), amend.go, amend_create.go; hdf-diff/go/amend/amend.go(+_test). 94.3% stmt cov on new file; lint clean both modules.

title: Wire export-contract test into CI/CD as merge gate
description:
Wire the export-contract test into CI so the regression cannot recur silently as new src/<subdir>/index.ts files are added in any hdf-libs package.

Required:
- Add `pnpm test:exports` step to the existing CI workflow(s) that run on PR and on push to main
- Step must run AFTER `pnpm build` (test asserts on dist/ output, requires a fresh build)
- Step must FAIL the PR check if any package's three-artifact contract is violated

Optional but valuable additions to consider:
- @arethetypeswrong/cli (`attw`) on the published tarball — checks types exports correctness across module systems (CommonJS/ESM/Node16 dual-package)
- `publint` — lints package.json for exports-field consistency with files on disk
- Both can run as additional CI steps; both catch a wider class of bugs than the custom test alone

Why this card:
The export-contract test we're adding (card hdf-libs-hq2z) is a regression guard. Without CI enforcement, a future contributor (or a future Claude session) can add src/<new-subdir>/index.ts, the test will pass locally only if explicitly run, and the same drift will recur. The CI step makes the contract enforced — every PR must pass the export-contract check.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] CI workflow file(s) updated with `pnpm test:exports` step
- [ ] Step runs after build, before merge gate
- [ ] PR fails when test fails (verified by intentionally breaking a package and confirming CI red)
- [ ] (Optional) attw + publint added if they fit the maintainer's tooling preference
- [ ] Documentation updated (CONTRIBUTING.md or similar) noting the contract for future contributors

Story points: sp:2

title: Fix hdf-mappings main-entry ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING (#45)
close_reason: No source change needed. Investigation revealed the design plan and upstream issue #45 prescribed adding `with { type: "json" }` to source — that approach is forbidden by the repo's existing policy (test/json-import-compatibility.test.ts:25-30, 76-96) because Vite strips import attributes during plugin analysis (Vite RFC #18534), leaving bare imports that raw Node rejects. Best practice for libraries consumed across multiple bundler ecosystems (Node, Vite, webpack, esbuild, Bun) is to inline JSON at build time — which tsdown already does. The published `@mitre/hdf-mappings@3.1.x` artifact bug closes by republishing with current source, which produces a self-contained dist/index.js with no JSON imports (verified by test/json-import-compatibility.test.ts line 122). See research summary in chat 2026-04-25 (Node ESM docs, Vite RFC #18534, tsdown docs).

title: Epic: fix package-boundary drift across hdf-libs (#43, #44, #45)
description:
Fix the package-boundary drift bug class across hdf-libs. Three artifacts (src/<subdir>/index.ts, tsdown.config.ts entry array, package.json exports map) have drifted in three packages, leaving utilities present in source but unreachable from any external consumer.

Confirmed bugs (filed upstream):

- mitre/hdf-libs#44 — hdf-diff matching/renderers + hdf-mappings 8 mapping subpaths unreachable
- mitre/hdf-libs#45 — hdf-mappings main-entry runtime fail (ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING — JSON imports missing 'with { type: "json" }')

Goal:
1. All published packages have reachable, runtime-importable subpath exports
2. Automated export-contract regression test exists (fails on this bug class for any package, any new src/ subdir, going forward)
3. All three upstream issues closed by the resulting PR

Strategy: TDD off main. Branch fix/package-boundary-drift. Write the export-contract test first; it must fail on all four known bugs. Fix one bug per logical commit. Final state: clean test pass, PR closes all three issues.

Design plan: docs/plans/2026-04-25-package-boundary-fix.md (in this repo).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Export-contract test exists and runs in CI (fails before fixes, passes after)
- [ ] Issues #43, #44, #45 closed by PR
- [ ] Fresh-consumer smoke test passes for hdf-utilities, hdf-diff, hdf-mappings

title: UX: rework hdf amend create TUI flow
description:
Major UX rework of hdf amend create interactive workflow:

1. ONE REQUIREMENT AT A TIME: Loop over single-requirement form (ID + type + reason + expiry + approver), then 'Add another?' prompt. Current bulk approach applies same metadata to all selected requirements.

2. ALL REQUIREMENTS, NOT JUST FAILS: When given a results file, show all requirements (not just failing) with their current status displayed next to the name. Users need to attest to notReviewed statuses too, and filtering to fails implies we want people to except their way out.

3. RELATIVE EXPIRY DATES: Support '1m', '6m', '1y', '90d' style input (like SAF CLI) in addition to YYYY-MM-DD. Compute absolute date from relative duration.

4. PAST DATE REJECTION: Validate that expiration date is in the future. Current code accepts past dates silently.

5. ADD INHERITED TYPE: Schema has 5 types (waiver, attestation, exception, poam, inherited) but TUI only shows 4. Add 'Inherited — control provided by another component' mapping to notApplicable.

6. FIX PLACEHOLDER EMAIL: Change issm@agency.gov to issm@acme.com.

7. EDITOR REDRAW BUG: Ctrl+E opens $EDITOR (nano by default), closing it redraws the field. This is a huh/bubbletea rendering artifact — investigate if fixable or document as known limitation.
close_reason: Full TUI rework: (1) one-requirement-at-a-time loop with 'Add another?' in standalone mode, per-requirement details in results mode; (2) shows ALL requirements with status symbols, not just fails; (3) relative expiry dates (30d, 3m, 1y); (4) rejects past dates; (5) added inherited amendment type → notApplicable; (6) placeholder email → issm@acme.com; (7) editor redraw documented as huh/bubbletea limitation. description:
Add control inheritance to HDF schemas. This is a fundamental concept in NIST SP 800-53 (common/hybrid/system-specific controls), FedRAMP (CRM), and OSCAL (by-component provided/inherited).

1. **system.schema.json**: Add Control_Designation type to $defs and controlDesignations[] array to the system document. Maps to OSCAL: providedBy ↔ by-components component-uuid with 'provided' responsibility; systemRef ↔ leveraged-authorizations; designation ↔ NIST SP 800-53 Appendix C designations; inherited amendment ↔ SAR findings with implementation-status: inherited.

title: Phase 1: Design hdf-component and hdf-data-flow schemas
description:
Design the new primitive schemas for hdf-component and hdf-data-flow.

hdf-component:
- componentId: UUID (RFC 4122), required in hdf-system, optional in hdf-results
- name: human-readable string, required
- externalIds: map of scheme→value (e.g. aws→i-1234, cmdb→ASSET-101)
- Polymorphic type system from current targets (host, containerImage, containerInstance, containerPlatform, cloudAccount, cloudResource, repository, application, artifact, network, database)
- All current target-specific fields retained per type
- labels, description
- sbom: embedded CycloneDX/SPDX object (full package inventory)
- sbomRef: optional URI to original SBOM document
- sbomFormat: cyclonedx | spdx
- baselineRefs, inputOverrides, targetSelector (from current system component)

hdf-data-flow:
- from: componentId (local)
- to: componentId (local) OR {systemRef, componentId} (cross-system) OR {external: true, description}
- protocol: string (http, https, socket, grpc, ssh, k8s-api, jdbc, etc.)
- port: number (optional)
- direction: unidirectional | bidirectional
- description: string
- authentication: string (optional)

CLI changes:
- hdf label gains --component-id and --generate-component-id flags
- hdf convert gains --component-id for pipeline stamping

Write JSON Schema files in hdf-schema/src/schemas/primitives/. Generate types. Write validation tests.

title: [EPIC] POSIX CLI refactor — flags over positionals, auto-detect, terminology
description:
Refactor hdf-cli to follow POSIX conventions: named flags instead of positional args for multi-value commands, auto-detect document types via fingerprint registry, and align terminology with v2 schemas (controls→requirements, profiles→baselines).

## Scope

### 1. hdf convert (breaking)
- Replace: hdf convert <src> to <dest> <input> [output]
- With: hdf convert <file> [--from <format>] [--to <format>] [-o output]
- Default --to is hdf. Omitting --from triggers fingerprint auto-detect.
- Refuse to guess below 0.8 confidence — require explicit --from.

### 2. hdf list (breaking)
- Replace: hdf list <what> <file>
- With: hdf list <file> [--type <item-type>]
- Auto-detect document type from file contents.
- Default (no --type): show summary overview for detected doc type.
- --type narrows to specific items (requirements, baselines, targets, components, interconnections, assessments, overrides, contents, groups).
- When listing requirements from results, annotate those with statusOverrides (waivers, attestations, etc.) with expiry info.
- Help text groups item types by document type for discoverability.

### 3. hdf amend apply (breaking)
- Replace: hdf amend apply <results> <amendments>
- With: hdf amend apply --results <file> --amendments <file> [-o output]

### 4. Terminology rename (non-breaking in flags, breaking in output)
- controls → requirements (all help text, output, flag names)
- profiles → baselines (all help text, output, flag names)
- Align with v2 schema naming throughout CLI.

## Not in scope
- Bulk file operations (separate bead hdf-libs-xm3)
- New CLI commands for system/plan/evidence (already implemented)
- Query command (already POSIX-compliant)

## Breaking change strategy
- Pre-release software, no published users
- Add deprecation warnings for old syntax? Or just change?

## Design principles
- Single positional arg = the input file (consistent across all commands)
- Everything else is a flag
- Auto-detect when possible, explicit flags when ambiguous
- Commands should read like English when flags are in conventional order
- Help text must make clear which --type values apply to which document types

title: Design hdf-comparison schema (formal diff document type)
description:
Design and formalize the hdf-comparison JSON schema as a new HDF document type.

Research found no industry standard for structured security assessment comparison:
- SARIF annotates results inline, no standalone diff document
- RFC 6902 is structural only, no security semantics
- No security tool (Snyk, Grype, DefectDojo, etc.) has a public diff schema

This positions HDF as the first formal schema for security assessment comparison.

Key design elements:
- Terraform-inspired before/after snapshots (not patches)
- SARIF-compatible state vocabulary (new, unchanged, updated, absent, fixed, regressed)
- Configurable matching strategies with confidence scores
- 4 comparison modes: temporal, baseline, fleet, multiSource
- Drift vs changes separation (Terraform pattern)
- Multi-scanner conflict preservation (Automerge pattern)
- HDF integrity integration (signed diffs for audit trails)

Design doc: docs/plans/2026-03-13-hdf-diff-schema-design.md
close_reason: Schema designed and implemented

- Wire into hdf-cli as `hdf diff scan1.json scan2.json` (already planned P3 in DESIGN-NOTES.md)
- Dual TS + Go implementation per hdf-libs pattern
- No OSCAL standard diff format exists — we define our own
- Also support SBOM diff: package added/removed/updated, new/resolved CVEs (match by purl)

Consumed by: Heimdall 3 comparison view, trend analysis, CI/CD pipelines via CLI.

title: Add XML entity expansion DoS protection to Go XML converters
description:
HIGH security finding: All 11 Go XML converters use encoding/xml with defaults. Go's XML parser is safe from XXE (ignores external entities) but vulnerable to billion-laughs internal entity expansion causing OOM. CLI's 50MB input limit provides coarse defense but library use has no protection.

Converters affected: nessus, burpsuite, fortify, veracode, dbprotect, netsparker, xccdf-results, zap, junit, hdf-to-xml, nikto

Options:
1. Wrap xml.NewDecoder input in io.LimitReader
2. Document Go XML safety properties explicitly
3. Add entity expansion detection pre-check

The CLI readInputFile already limits to 50MB which bounds the worst case.

title: Add omitempty tags to Go type generation for discriminated unions

- Without omitempty, Go marshals all nil fields as null
- Result: Host target outputs 37 fields (35 nulls) instead of 7 relevant fields

Solution:
- Update hdf-schema type generation to add omitempty tags to optional fields
- Ensures only populated fields appear in JSON output
- Matches schema semantic intent of discriminated unions

Approach (TDD):
1. Write test that asserts omitempty tags exist on generated types
2. Write test that validates marshaled JSON only contains non-null fields
3. Update quicktype generation or post-processing to add omitempty
4. Verify all converters produce cleaner output

Affects:
- hdf-schema/src/generators/go.ts (type generation)
- All converters using Target, EvaluatedBaseline, etc.
- Should be backward compatible (omitting nulls does not break consumers)

title: Normalize Go converter custom-layout time.Parse results to UTC
description: After the TS timestamp sweep (hdf-libs-d2ql), TS *-to-hdf converters emit UTC via parseTimestamp, and most Go peers use hdfutil.ParseTimestamp (now .UTC().Truncate(ms)). But ~9 Go converters parse tool timestamps with custom time.Parse layouts and never .UTC() the result, so for a NON-zero-offset source they emit offset-preserving timestamps while their TS peers emit Z — a residual Go/TS divergence (zero-offset/Z/zone-less sources are unaffected; Go renders +0000 as Z). Sites: burpsuite-to-hdf/go:104,108; dbprotect-to-hdf/go:128; grype-to-hdf/go:611,613; netsparker-to-hdf/go:155; scoutsuite-to-hdf/go:198,289; sonarqube-to-hdf/go:499; trufflehog-to-hdf/go:169; veracode-to-hdf/go:778; zap-to-hdf/go:74. Fix: wrap each parse result in .UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond) (these custom layouts handle formats hdfutil.ParseTimestamp does not, so keep the layout, just normalize the result). Snapshot tests normalize timestamps so no fixture churn. See hdf-timestamp-canonical-utc memory.
notes: [2026-06-28] DONE — commit e16989b on branch fix/go-custom-timestamp-utc, rebased onto merged main (post-#115, base 8c815c0), 1 commit ahead. 8 Go converters (burpsuite/dbprotect/netsparker/scoutsuite/sonarqube/trufflehog/veracode/zap) wrap custom time.Parse results in .UTC().Truncate(ms). Note: snapshot tests normalize timestamps so the 8 have no explicit UTC assertion (relies on convention+docs).

title: hdf convert: legacy InSpec (hdf@1) input fails for non-hdf export targets (#104 pt1)
description:
Issue #104 part 1. Legacy InSpec exec-json (HDF v1, profiles-shaped, no baselines) is only upgraded to modern HDF when --to hdf. Root cause: CLI input-normalization gap. --from hdf@1 --to hdf works (hdfVersionConverter upgrades); --from hdf@1 --to <export> and auto-detected legacyhdf --to <export> do not.

Fix (systemic, maintainer-chosen): in the convert flow, upgrade HDF v1 input to modern HDF (hdfversion.TransformHDF 1->2, == legacyhdf-to-hdf) before any non-hdf export converter. Covers explicit --from hdf@1 and auto-detected legacyhdf, all export targets. No converter changes -> no Go/TS parity concern.

Part 2 (poam converter 'removed') confirmed NOT a bug by reporter: POA&M now sourced from hdf-amendments by design.

title: feat/rev-5: NIST 800-53 Rev 5 initiative (rev-aware mappings + default)
description:
Split out from hdf-libs-5sbx / issue #96. The CCI-derivation + TS NIST-split fix shipped separately (branch fix/issue-96-aws-config-mappings, commit 059313b). This bead is the remaining NIST *coverage* half.

## Problem
hdf-mappings/{go,src}/awsconfig/awsconfig-mappings.json is a 106-row table, ALL tagged Rev:4. AWS Config now has 400+ managed rules and AWS publishes a Rev 5 pack. Rules not in the table emit no NIST (and thus no derived CCI). Issue #96's reporter likely hit an unmapped rule.

## Authoritative source (verified)
The table's Rev:4 tag shows it was derived from AWS 'Operational Best Practices for NIST 800-53 Rev 4' conformance pack. Authoritative, machine-readable sources:
- AWS Operational Best Practices conformance pack templates (Rev 4 + Rev 5) — each managed rule listed under the NIST control(s) it satisfies.
- GitHub mirrors: awslabs/aws-config-rules, aws-samples/aws-config-conformance-packs.
This is AWS's own mapping, so expanding from it is legitimate sourcing, not fabrication (satisfies the data-integrity rule).

## Scope
- Pull Rev 4 (refresh) + Rev 5 mappings; parse rule SourceIdentifier/name -> NIST control list.
- Regenerate awsconfig-mappings.json with the Rev field; keep both the Go embed (go/awsconfig/) and the TS copy (src/awsconfig/) in sync (they are duplicated — verify both).
- Document provenance (source URL + retrieval date) in a README or header note.
- Verify a sample of regenerated rows against AWS source; spot-check converter output.

## Correctness bar
Wrong NIST mappings are worse than gaps. Source from a machine-readable AWS artifact and verify; do NOT loosely scrape HTML.

## Related nuance
The NIST->CCI table (hdf-mappings cci/nist-cci-mappings.json) is a 21-entry curated set, so expanded NIST coverage only increases derived CCI where new controls fall in those 21. A separate, larger effort would be building a comprehensive NIST->CCI inverse from the 3551-entry DISA CCI list — out of scope here.
acceptance_criteria: awsconfig-mappings.json expanded with authoritative Rev 4-refresh + Rev 5 rule->NIST mappings; Go embed and TS copy in sync; provenance documented; sample verified against AWS source

title: UTF-8 BOM breaks CLI input across all commands (detect, convert, validate, query, diff)
description:
Confirmed via PR #105 Copilot review. readInputFile (hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/input.go) does not strip a leading UTF-8 BOM, and neither do the registry auto-detect dispatchers (registry/fingerprint.go, shared/typescript/fingerprint.ts) nor the converters' own parsers. Go json.Unmarshal and JS JSON.parse both reject a leading BOM, so BOM-prefixed (Windows-generated) files fail:

- Auto-detect: DetectFamily strips the BOM for classification and returns FamilyJSON, but the subsequent json.Unmarshal runs on the original BOM bytes and fails -> 'could not auto-detect'.
- Convert with explicit --from: the converter's own parse (e.g. trufflehog parseFindings) fails -> 'failed to parse NDJSON line: invalid character'.
- Same blindness in validate/query/list/diff which all call readInputFile.

A detection-only BOM fix is harmful in isolation: it makes auto-detect succeed and then conversion fail (worse failure mode), so detection and the converter/input layers must be fixed together. The right chokepoint is likely readInputFile (CLI) plus the registry dispatchers (library robustness for TS/heimdall consumers that pass raw input).

## Repro
printf '\xEF\xBB\xBF' > /tmp/b.ndjson; cat hdf-converters/converters/trufflehog-to-hdf/fixtures/input/ndjson-input.ndjson >> /tmp/b.ndjson; hdf convert /tmp/b.ndjson -o /tmp/o.json
# Detected: TruffleHog (confidence: 100%) then 'conversion failed: ... invalid character'

## Scope
- Strip leading UTF-8 BOM at readInputFile (covers convert/validate/query/list/diff)
- Strip in registry Go + TS detect dispatchers for direct library consumers
- Tests: BOM-prefixed JSON, NDJSON, and XML for detect + convert; BOM-prefixed HDF for validate/query
- Verify schema-validation gatekeeper (input.go parseHDFResults) tolerates the stripped input
acceptance_criteria: BOM-prefixed JSON/NDJSON/XML inputs auto-detect AND convert; BOM-prefixed HDF validates/queries; covered by tests in Go and TS
notes:
Empirically verified blast radius by format (leading UTF-8 BOM only; most tools emit no BOM):
- JSON/NDJSON: HARD FAIL both paths. Auto-detect returns 'could not auto-detect'; explicit --from fails in converter (json.Unmarshal rejects BOM). e.g. trufflehog.
- XML: detection FAILS (auto-detect can't classify/fingerprint the BOM-prefixed preamble), BUT explicit --from WORKS — Go encoding/xml tolerates a leading BOM. Verified end-to-end with junit fixture.
- CSV: SILENT CORRUPTION, not a hard fail — Go encoding/csv folds the BOM into the first header field ('﻿col1'), so header-name matching breaks and output is silently wrong. CSV is excluded from auto-detect by design, so only the --from path applies.
Implication: fix must strip BOM at the input chokepoint (covers all three) AND in the registry dispatchers (so XML/JSON auto-detect classifies BOM files). CSV warrants its own test asserting clean first-header.
close_reason: Fixed on branch fix/bom-input-handling (commit 674ddb0): strip leading UTF-8 BOM at readInputFile chokepoint + Go/TS registry dispatchers. Regression tests for BOM JSON/XML detect (registry), readInputFile strip, and CLI e2e for JSON/XML/CSV convert + HDF validate. Live-verified with rebuilt binary across all formats. NOTE: BOM+NDJSON combined path covered once PR 105 (NDJSON) merges to main.

title: CLI schema gate uniformity: route remaining raw load sites through loadAndValidateHDFDoc / parseHDF*
description:
The m58u CLI schema gate (PR #100) was advertised as uniform but several CLI sites still load HDF docs raw via direct `json.Unmarshal`, bypassing the validation gate:

1. `hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/threshold.go:35,64` — `json.Unmarshal(data, &results)` directly into `hdf.HDFResults`; should call `parseHDFResults`.
2. `hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/evidence_verify.go:77,162` — reads evidence package + nested results raw; should use `loadAndValidateHDFDoc(data, "evidencePackage")` and `parseHDFResults` respectively.
3. `hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/evidence_export.go:52` — reads evidence package raw.
4. `hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/amend_create.go:161` and `hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/amend_headless.go:390` — read HDF Results raw for amend-from-results.
5. `hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/plan_create.go:88` — reads a known-HDF system doc; only the OUTPUT side is currently gated, not the input.

Each site should either route through the appropriate gate helper OR carry a comment documenting why it's exempt (as `computeCompleteness` in `evidence_build.go` does — that one walks raw JSON intentionally for partial-input metric collection).

Risk if shipped as-is: users hit the validation gate inconsistently — `hdf system set` rejects a malformed doc, but `hdf threshold`, `hdf evidence verify`, and `hdf amend create` silently accept the same input and produce undefined behavior downstream.

title: [bug] aws-config NIST mapping coverage + missing CCI tag emission
description:
GitHub issue #96 reports 'NIST and CCI tags absent from `hdf fetch aws-config` output'. Investigation:

## NIST: WORKS for mapped rules
The converter (Go and TS) calls `awsconfigmap.NISTControls(sourceIdentifier)` and emits `tags.nist` whenever a rule has an entry in the 637-row mapping at `hdf-mappings/{go,src}/awsconfig/awsconfig-mappings.json`. Spot-checked on `multi-rule.json` fixture: emits e.g. `{nist: ['AC-2(j)', 'IA-2(1)(11)']}` correctly.

The user's complaint likely surfaces from rules NOT in the 637-row table. The table is large but not exhaustive against the full AWS Config catalog. Coverage gaps are real; user-facing message should be 'submit specific rule IDs / SourceIdentifiers you need mapped' rather than 'NIST mapping is broken'.

## CCI: NOT emitted
The aws-config converter never emits `tags.cci`. AWS Config rules don't have native CCI references, but we could derive them via NIST -> CCI lookup (cci package in hdf-mappings). Currently no derivation happens.

## Proposed work
1. **Verify reproducibility** with the issue reporter: ask which specific rules they saw uncovered. If they have rule IDs without NIST mappings, expand the mapping JSON (additive, no schema impact).
2. **Decide CCI policy**: should aws-config (and other NIST-mapped converters that lack native CCI) derive CCI from NIST? If yes, do it as a shared helper in `hdf-converters/shared` so it applies uniformly. If no, document the decision (NIST tags are sufficient for AWS Config; CCI is a DoD-specific layer that may not be meaningful here).
3. **Update issue #96** with the findings either way.

## Out of scope
- 'Heimdall / SPARC / saf CLI cannot use the filters' angle in the GitHub issue. Those downstream apps aren't on the new schemas yet; that's tracked separately.

References GitHub issue #96
close_reason: Decomposed into two atomic PRs. CCI derivation + the pre-existing TS NIST-pipe-split bug fix: committed as 059313b on branch fix/issue-96-aws-config-mappings (PR pending). NIST coverage expansion: tracked in hdf-libs-9sh5 (branch fix/aws-config-nist-coverage). GitHub issue #96 stays open until both ship in a release (per issue-lifecycle policy).

title: Fix TS importers emitting schema-invalid HDF Results (mostly missing startTime)
description:
Discovered during hdf-libs-nrr4 (TS importer schema-validation sweep): 14 TS importers emit HDF Results that fail validators.validateResults. The dominant bug is missing required field `results[].startTime` on Evaluated_Result. Two converters have additional issues.

Affected importers (validation error per converter):

| Importer | Validation error |
|---|---|
| checkov-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing |
| ckl-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing (all 6 reqs) |
| cklb-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing (all 6 reqs) |
| cyclonedx-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing (all 3 reqs) |
| gosec-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing (all reqs, 150+ results) |
| jfrog-xray-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing (all 17 reqs) |
| junit-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing (both reqs) |
| msft-defender-cloud-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing (both reqs) |
| msft-defender-endpoint-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing |
| neuvector-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing (all 8 reqs) |
| oscal-to-hdf (SAR) | baselines.1.requirements: minItems 1; baselines.2.requirements: minItems 1 (empty additional baselines) |
| prisma-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing (both baselines) |
| snyk-to-hdf | results[].startTime missing (all 8 reqs) |
| xccdf-results-to-hdf | baselines.0.requirements.0.descriptions: minItems 1 AND results[].startTime missing |

Why this matters:
The Go-side converters emit `startTime` (Go validators pass) but the TS importers don't. This was silent until nrr4 wired schema validation into TS importer tests. CLI downstream of any of these would emit schema-invalid HDF when run with the TS path.

Scope:
- Fix each TS importer to emit `startTime` on every Evaluated_Result. Patterns vary: some Go converters use a doc-level scan timestamp, others use per-finding timestamps from the source format. Mirror the Go logic per-importer.
- For oscal-to-hdf: skip empty baselines or emit at least a placeholder requirement (mirror Go behavior).
- For xccdf-results-to-hdf: also fill the required `descriptions` array.
- Add `expectValidResults` call to each importer test in the same place the nrr4 sweep would have added it.

Discovery: nrr4 sweep, 2026-06-15. Helper at hdf-converters/test/helpers/expectValidHdf.ts.
notes:
FIX committed 83fbf13 on branch fix/je13-ts-importer-starttime (awaiting push). All 14 affected importers now emit schema-required results[].startTime in BOTH TS and Go.

Root cause: schema's Requirement_Result requires startTime; TS omitted the optional field (invalid), Go emitted zero-value 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z (valid-but-meaningless placeholder via non-pointer time.Time).

Fix: emit a meaningful startTime — real source timestamp where the format carries one (cyclonedx metadata.timestamp, junit testsuite timestamp, msft-defender-endpoint firstActivityDateTime/createdDateTime, oscal result.start, xccdf rr.time/start-time), else one conversion-time value per conversion (gosec/snyk/checkov/neuvector/prisma/ckl/cklb/msft-defender-cloud). Special cases: oscal-sar now SKIPS zero-finding results (mirrors Go) instead of emitting empty baselines (requirements.minItems=1); xccdf-results guarantees non-empty descriptions. ckl/cklb fixed at the shared checklist builder (shared/{go,typescript}/checklist) — single locus, no per-converter duplication.

Tests: expectValidResults wired into all 14 importer test files (schema-validates a success path, prevents regression) + fallback-path tests added (oscal no-start, xccdf bare-rule, junit no-ts, msft-endpoint no-activity-time) to hold branch coverage >=90%. Full hdf-converters gate green: TS 2733+ pass, Go all pass, eslint+golangci-lint 0, tsc clean, branch coverage 90.01%.

Done pending merge/release.

title: Make hdf diff JSON output schema-compliant against hdf-comparison
description:
Discovered during hdf-libs-m58u: the CLI's diff JSON output uses field names matching the hdf-comparison schema but several shapes drift from the schema. Validation against hdf-comparison fails:

1. `componentDiffs` entries (CLI's per-component summaries: Name, BaselineRefs, Summary, OldCompliance, NewCompliance, ComplianceDelta) lack the schema-required `state` field. Schema's componentDiffs is a state diff (new/absent/unchanged/updated), not a per-component compliance summary.

2. Nil slices (Sources, BaselineDiffs, etc.) serialize as JSON `null` instead of empty arrays, but the schema requires arrays.

3. The CLI's `diffRequirement.ChangeReasons` and `FieldChanges` likewise serialize as null when empty.

Scope:
- Either rename the CLI's componentDiffs to something the schema doesn't constrain (e.g. componentSummaries) and move it to extensions, OR add proper per-component state tracking and produce schema-conformant componentDiffs.
- Initialize all nil slices to empty slices before serialization (Sources, BaselineDiffs, ChangeReasons, FieldChanges).
- Re-enable the validateHDFOutput call in outputDiffJSON (see diff.go).

The m58u bead intentionally skipped this validation because untangling these shape discrepancies is a meaningful refactor beyond uniform-gate coverage.

Affected files:
- hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/diff.go — outputDiffJSON, diffResult, componentSummary, engineResultToDiffResult.

Test fixtures to refresh after fix:
- hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/diff_coverage_test.go TestDiffCoverage_RenderDiffOutput
- hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/diff_test.go TestDiffCommand_SystemFlag_JSON, TestDiffCommand_SystemFlag_ComplianceValues

Other agent's parallel branch (feat/hdf-cli-schema-gates-for-system-plan-evidence-comparison) deferred this and filed qcg7; my m58u branch shipped it inline.

title: Validate aws-securityhub fetcher against a real AWS Security Hub instance
description:
The aws-securityhub fetcher (commit f4f6c55) was built and tested against an interface-based SDK mock that synthesizes GetFindings + DescribeHub responses. The mock contract is grounded in the AWS SDK's typed command shapes; no validation against a live AWS account has been performed.

Live test surface:
- VerifyCredentials round-trip (DescribeHub) with real IAM creds.
- GetFindings pagination across an account with realistic finding volume (>100, to exercise the NextToken plumbing).
- ASFF response shape matches what asff-to-hdf expects after the heimdall2 port — Standards ARNs, Compliance.Status, Resources.Details patterns evolve over time; the fixture-based ASFF tests may not reflect current Security Hub output.
- TLS path: SDK handles its own TLS, but verify that --ca-cert / --insecure flags work when an enterprise proxy is in the chain.

This bead overlaps with hdf-libs-sokk (validate asff-to-hdf converter against real findings) — sokk and this bead can be satisfied together with a single AWS account spin-up.

## Access provisioning

Per /tmp/aws-securityhub-fixture-plan.md (drafted earlier this session):
- Minimum IAM policy: 3 actions — securityhub:GetFindings, securityhub:DescribeHub, securityhub:GetEnabledStandards.
- Provision a dedicated IAM user with that policy + access key for local dev (Option A in the plan). Migrate to assumable role if the same account ever sees CI use.
- Seed findings via batch-import-findings to avoid waiting for real standards population, OR enable AWS Foundational Security Best Practices and wait 24h.

## Validation checks

- `hdf fetch aws-securityhub --region us-east-1 --check` succeeds with valid keys, fails cleanly on rotated keys.
- `hdf fetch aws-securityhub --region us-east-1 -o /tmp/out.json` produces an HDF document; `hdf validate /tmp/out.json` passes.
- `hdf fetch aws-securityhub --region us-east-1 --format raw -o /tmp/asff.json`; manually inspect for unhandled fields the schema-evolved Security Hub now emits (FindingProviderFields, multi-standard Compliance arrays, etc).
- Cross-check: `hdf convert --from asff /tmp/asff.json -o /tmp/via-convert.json; diff /tmp/out.json /tmp/via-convert.json` — structural diff empty (timestamps will differ).

## Error-path checks
- 401-equivalent (rotated keys / wrong region) — error doesn't leak AK/SK values
- Throttle error path (synthesize via heavy parallel requests if account allows)
- --ca-cert path with a private CA proxy
- --insecure path works (with stderr warning)

## Outcomes

- If all green: append a comment to `fetchers/aws-securityhub/go/aws_securityhub.go` documenting the AWS SDK version + date validated against. Close this bead.
- If divergence: file targeted follow-up beads naming each gap.

title: Migrate hdf verify {splunk,tenable-sc} to hdf fetch <tool> --check shape
description:
The aws-securityhub fetcher (commit f4f6c55) ships its credential-probe capability as a `--check` flag on `hdf fetch aws-securityhub` rather than a sibling `hdf verify <tool>` parent command. The taxonomy reasoning: verb-first top-level parents are a real commitment, and grouping tool-network operations under a single parent ("hdf fetch <tool>") keeps the top-level surface tighter.

`hdf verify splunk` (commit 16c7fcc) and `hdf verify tenable-sc` (commit c714424) on `feat/splunk-fetcher` predate this taxonomy decision. They need to migrate to `hdf fetch <tool> --check` to keep the CLI consistent.

## Work

- Remove the `hdf verify` parent command (`verify.go`).
- Remove `verify_splunk.go` and `verify_splunk_test.go`.
- Remove `verify_tenable_sc.go` and `verify_tenable_sc_test.go`.
- Add a `--check` flag to `hdf fetch splunk` that calls SplunkFetcher.VerifyCredentials. Mirror the aws-securityhub --check semantics: exit 0 + "Splunk credentials verified" on stderr, non-zero with clear error otherwise.
- Add a `--check` flag to `hdf fetch tenable-sc` that calls TenableSCFetcher.VerifyCredentials. Same shape.
- Update hdf-cli/README.md to remove the verify TOC entries and document --check under each fetch subsection.
- Update hdf-cli/cmd/hdf/cmd/fetch.go Long description to mention --check as a generic flag pattern across all fetch leaves.
- Update root.go to drop NewVerifyCmd registration.

## Sequencing

Depends on `feat/splunk-fetcher` merging first (gives us the verify commands to migrate). If `feat/aws-securityhub-fetcher` merges before `feat/splunk-fetcher`, the merge of feat/splunk-fetcher will carry verify commands that this PR removes; the migration PR cleans up after both ship.

## Verification

- `pnpm check` exits 0
- Manual CLI smoke tests:
  - `hdf fetch splunk --url X --check` ≡ old `hdf verify splunk --url X`
  - `hdf fetch tenable-sc --url X --check` ≡ old `hdf verify tenable-sc --url X`
- `hdf --help` no longer shows `verify` as a top-level command

title: Validate tenable-sc fetcher against a live Tenable.SC instance
description:
The tenable-sc fetcher (hdf-libs-0lm0, commit c714424) was built and tested against `httptest.Server` mocks that synthesize Tenable.SC's documented API response shapes. The mock contract is grounded in heimdall2's `tenable_util.ts` port and Tenable's published API docs, but no validation against a live instance has been performed. This bead tracks that follow-up spot-check.

The tenable-sc fetcher is read-only on our side (no push), so the live test surface is: (a) does VerifyCredentials round-trip work with real API keys, (b) does the `response.usable` list envelope match our parse, (c) does the download endpoint return raw .nessus XML or a zip wrapping it (or sometimes both, per the docs), and (d) do the converted HDF results validate cleanly.

Blocker for landing this is access to a Tenable.SC instance plus credentials — Tenable.SC is a licensed on-prem product, no free tier. See `/tmp/tenable-sc-live-test-plan.md` for the access options (MITRE-internal, vendor eval, or skip).

## Access options (whichever is fastest)
- Existing MITRE-operated Tenable.SC instance with a read-only API user provisioned for us. **Best path** — ask MITRE IT.
- 30-day vendor eval — Tenable issues a trial license through sales engagement. Requires standing up a RHEL-equivalent VM and a separate Nessus scanner. Heavy for a one-shot spot-check.
- Tenable.IO does NOT substitute — different API surface (`/scans/...` instead of `/rest/scanResult/...`), different auth shape. Out of scope.

## Provisioning
- API user with the built-in **Auditor** role (read-only across the org, can list and download scan results). Avoid Administrator (overprivileged) and Credential Manager (wrong scope — manages stored target credentials, not scan results).
- Group assigned to a group with visibility into the repositories / scan zones holding the scans to fetch.
- API keys minted by the user under **My Account → API Keys → Generate API Keys**. Secret is shown once.
- At least one completed scan in a repository the user can read. For a fresh instance: Basic Network Scan against 127.0.0.1 finishes in a few minutes.

## Validation checks
- `hdf verify tenable-sc --url <url>` succeeds with valid keys, fails cleanly on rotated keys.
- `hdf fetch tenable-sc --url <url> --scan-id <id> -o /tmp/out.json` produces an HDF Results document.
- `hdf validate /tmp/out.json` passes schema.
- Both response shapes work — raw .nessus XML AND zip-wrapped — by inspecting which shape the live server returns (`hdf fetch ... --format raw -o /tmp/scan.bin; file /tmp/scan.bin`). The fetcher sniffs the first 4 bytes either way, but knowing which shape Tenable.SC actually serves in practice is worth recording.
- Cross-check: `hdf fetch ... --format raw -o /tmp/scan.nessus; hdf convert --from nessus /tmp/scan.nessus -o /tmp/via-convert.json; diff /tmp/out.json /tmp/via-convert.json` — structural diff should be empty (timestamps will differ). Confirms fetcher and converter agree end-to-end.

## Error-path checks
- 403 on download with a user role that lacks scan-download permission — error message should be unambiguous, never leak key material.
- 404 on a nonexistent scan ID — error includes the scan ID.
- 401 with rotated/invalid keys — error includes "unauthorized," NOT the key values.
- Corporate CA support: `--ca-cert /path/to/corp-ca.pem` works for internal instances; `--insecure` warns to stderr.

## Outcomes
- If all green: append a comment to `fetchers/tenable-sc/go/tenable_sc.go` documenting the Tenable.SC version + date validated against. Close this bead.
- If divergence: file targeted follow-up beads naming each gap (unhandled response field, unexpected download shape, error path leaking key material, etc.). Do not silently patch — divergences are real signal about the mock contract.

## Reference
- Plan doc: `/tmp/tenable-sc-live-test-plan.md` (notes from 2026-06-12; not committed)
- Precedent: hdf-libs-sokk (same shape, ASFF/Security Hub)
- Fetcher commit: c714424
- Epic parent: hdf-libs-34aa (issue #86)
